LESSON: BIRTH OF PROPHET

Grade: Grade 1
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: SIIRAH (Life of
Topic 3.1: Birth of Prophet

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Birth of Prophet. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Where was the Prophet a) narrate the event  Learners are guided to name the place (S.A.W.) born?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain what Birth of Prophet means in simple pupil language
2. give 3 correct examples of Birth of Prophet from Kenya
3. practise Birth of Prophet in clear steps
4. apply Birth of Prophet in one real-life situation this week

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: BIRTH OF PROPHET
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Birth of Prophet helps you succeed in ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: BIRTH OF PROPHET
Study Birth of Prophet like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Explain what Birth of Prophet means in simple pupil language

What this means
In this part you learn to explain what Birth of Prophet means in simple pupil language. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain what Birth of Prophet means in simple pupil language.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Birth of Prophet” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain what Birth of Prophet means in simple pupil language. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Give 3 correct examples of Birth of Prophet from Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to give 3 correct examples of Birth of Prophet from Kenya. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: give 3 correct examples of Birth of Prophet from Kenya.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Birth of Prophet in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can give 3 correct examples of Birth of Prophet from Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Practise Birth of Prophet in clear steps

What this means
In this part you learn to practise Birth of Prophet in clear steps. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise Birth of Prophet in clear steps.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise Birth of Prophet in clear steps. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Apply Birth of Prophet in one real-life situation this week

What this means
In this part you learn to apply Birth of Prophet in one real-life situation this week. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply Birth of Prophet in one real-life situation this week.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Birth of Prophet” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply Birth of Prophet in one real-life situation this week. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Birth of Prophet is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Birth of Prophet” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: explain what Birth of Prophet means in simple pupil language)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Birth of Prophet in your own words. (skill: give 3 correct examples of Birth of Prophet from Kenya)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: practise Birth of Prophet in clear steps)

Example 4: Show how “Birth of Prophet” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: apply Birth of Prophet in one real-life situation this week)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Birth of Prophet to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain what Birth of Prophet means in simple pupil language.
3. Practise this skill: give 3 correct examples of Birth of Prophet from Kenya.
4. Practise this skill: practise Birth of Prophet in clear steps.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Birth of Prophet from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Birth of Prophet: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 1 learner study Birth of Prophet?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Where was the Prophet a) narrate the event  Learners are guided to name the place (S.A.W.) born?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Birth of Prophet means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain what Birth of Prophet means in simple pupil language.
5. Be able to: give 3 correct examples of Birth of Prophet from Kenya.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
